content: If you are currently taking masoprolol, it is important to contact your doctor to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Masoprolol is prescribed to treat skin growths caused by sun exposure. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information regarding its applications. Masoprolol is available as a cream intended for topical use. Typically, it is applied to the skin twice daily, in the morning and evening, for a duration of 28 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to clarify any directions you do not understand. Use masoprolol exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less of the medication, nor use it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If you are applying this medication to a child’s diaper area, avoid using tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these can increase the absorption of masoprolol, potentially leading to harmful effects. Before application, thoroughly clean the affected area, allow it to dry, and gently rub the cream into the skin until most of it disappears. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication. Before using masoprolol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to masoprolol, sulfites, or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using masoprolol, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and take precautions such as wearing protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as masoprolol may increase your skin’s sensitivity to sunlight. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Masoprolol may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: burning, redness, itching, dry skin, or roughness/wrinkling. If you experience severe side effects such as bleeding, blistering, or a skin rash, contact your doctor immediately. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Masoprolol is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Be aware that this medication can stain clothing and bedding. To minimize staining, rub the cream into your skin thoroughly and apply it at least two hours before bedtime. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Inform your doctor if your skin condition worsens or does not improve.
